newsitem.title: USA: NCR sees higher net, but below analysts' expectations.
newsitem.headline: NCR sees higher net, but below analysts' expectations.

text.p: NCR Corp. said Tuesday its earnings for the second quarter will likely fall short of analysts' estimates, primarily because of weak services revenues and disappointing orders for its hardware systems.

The computer systems and services company, which was spun off from AT&T at the end of last year, said it expected improved results for the period compared with a year ago, when it lost $18 million, or 18 cents per share.
However, orders are expected to increase, making for the sixth consecutive quarter that orders have gained on a year-over-year basis.
NCR said it remains optimistic it can have higher orders and revenues in its core businesses, an improvement in operating income and an improvement in per-share results for the full year.

But industry analysts' expectations for the quarter will not likely be met, the company said, primarily because of revenue and gross margin pressures for services and an expected shortfall in computer systems orders and revenue, compared with last year.

To help offset the shortfall, NCR said it is recruiting and training nearly 800 new employees worldwide this year to help improve its computer and associated services revenues. More than half of the new people will be involved in computer sales.
NCR, once the focus of AT&T's effort to become a leader in the computer industry, is a maker of transaction processing systems, automated teller machines, scanners and point of sale terminals.
NCR's stock was down $1.125 at $29.125 on the New York Stock Exchange.
